target_problem: construct missing outputs in deterministic polynomial time for exact-stretch essential ternary signed-majority NC0_3 circuits
conditional_implication: For every explicit circuit C:{0,1}^n->{0,1}^m with m>n whose outputs are essential ternary signed-majority gates on three distinct inputs, inclusion-minimal surplus extraction, a Rado/frame-matroid pair transversal, and a constant six-path unicyclic kernel yield a deterministic polynomial-time missing-output construction.
frontier_reason: V107 removes V106's repair-distance exponent for the full essential signed-majority orbit. The proof reduces a minimally positive-surplus block to rank-tight unbalanced-unicyclic frame components and handles the sole same-component case by a computer-assisted constant kernel with 16,032 exact signed/polarity instances.

closed_route: bounded pair-repair distance as the necessary signed-majority parameter
surviving_route: attack the remaining MUX/bijunctive 0x1b orbit and then recompute the post-V100/V101 residual frontier before testing any published lower-bound transfer
current_gap: V107 covers only essential ternary signed-majority outputs. The MUX/bijunctive 0x1b orbit remains outside the unrestricted polynomial-time laboratory coverage, so general NC0_3-Avoid and P versus NP remain unresolved.
stop_rule: Do not promote V108 for another signed-majority finite census. Require a scalable theorem for the remaining MUX/bijunctive orbit, a rigorous reduction of that orbit to solved structure, or a hardness/barrier result that changes the global range-avoidance frontier.
external_validation_target: specialist review of the Rado/frame-matroid construction, the six-path computer-assisted kernel proof, exact-stretch signed-majority range avoidance prior art, and proof-assistant or independently implemented replay of the 16032 kernel cases
